title: Control-room journey gate
description: Objective: prove J1-J6 end to end against a real daemon with accessibility, degraded, cursor-gap, approval, graph, and recovery fixtures. Deliverable: Playwright journey evidence at one exact commit. NOT in scope: portability adapters or GA claims. Hard dependencies: every M3 surface and Graph operator journeys. Owned paths: tests/e2e/control-room/** and release evidence paths only. Verification: pnpm test:e2e.
definitionOfDone: All pinned J1-J6 acceptance criteria and twenty scenario-matrix cases pass.
Truth, provenance, keyboard, narrow-window, loading, degraded, and latency invariants pass globally.
No action exists without an allowed daemon command and no transcript enters clean review.
Playwright gate exits 0 at one exact commit.
taskRails: The standalone control room displays daemon truth and nextAllowedCommands; it never derives authority, readiness, or evidence strength.
Every fact is text/icon/color encoded, keyboard accessible, provenance-drillable, and honest under degraded data.
IDE adapters remain thin optional launch/discover/embed shells with no product logic. Keep modules below 400 lines; explicit owned paths only.

implementationPlan.description:
SCOPE THE GATE HONESTLY (read-only design step). This is the decision the whole task turns on, and it is already made — implement it, do not relitigate it.

COVER: the journeys whose surfaces actually exist, driven through the real Playwright browser against the real built bundle.
RECORD AS TYPED UNKNOWN: every graph scenario, naming task-779d6804 as the missing owner.

CLAUSE 2 IS THE FENCE. A graph journey driven against GraphPlaceholder would be "a proof that only proves the shapes", which Clause 2 calls worse than no proof, because it retires the scenario while certifying nothing. Equally forbidden: a narrowed DoD presented as complete, a mock-backed graph journey, and authority reimplemented inside the test. NEVER create a component to give a scenario something to find — a stub carrying a real cr.graph.* or cr.banner.revision id is fabricated evidence, and the frame already refuses to do this.

ENUMERATE THE SCENARIO MATRIX EXPLICITLY as a frozen list, each entry carrying status COVERED or UNKNOWN plus, for UNKNOWN, its missing input and owning task. DoD 1 names twenty scenario cases: the count must be visible and asserted, so a reader can see at a glance how many are genuinely covered versus recorded. A gate that silently drops the graph cases would read as complete.

Three ids the governor notes NOW EXIST and therefore move into COVERED — verify each on disk yourself before relying on it: cr.runs (runs/runs-surface.tsx), cr.resources (resources/resources-surface.tsx), cr.banner.circuitbreaker (shell/circuit-breaker-banner.tsx).

THE DEFECT IS ON A SECOND AXIS THE LEDGER NEVER MODELLED. journey-coverage.ts records the twenty SPEC SECTION 12 SCENARIOS plus one inherited obligation (LATENCY_RECORD). DoD 2 is a DIFFERENT list — seven named INVARIANTS: truth, provenance, keyboard, narrow-window, loading, degraded, latency. Nothing in the repository ever enumerated that list. Five are asserted in journeys.spec.ts, latency was recorded only because it arrived as an inherited obligation, and loading fell through the gap between the two axes. That is why the omission was silent: there was no list for it to be missing FROM.

DECISION, and it is deliberately wider than the single record QA demanded:
  1. LOADING_RECORD lands in journey-coverage.ts beside LATENCY_RECORD — exactly the location and shape QA named. cause SURFACE_NOT_COMPOSED, non-empty missingInput naming ControlRoomPreview, an owner.
  2. The seven-invariant DoD 2 ledger lands as a NEW module, journey-invariants.ts, enumerating all seven with each COVERED entry naming the browser test that proves it and each UNKNOWN carrying cause/missingInput/owner.

WHY (2) AND NOT JUST (1). Recording only loading fixes the named hole and leaves the mechanism that produced it intact. Today nothing binds DoD 2's list to the tests: delete the keyboard test from journeys.spec.ts and no assertion anywhere notices, exactly as nothing noticed loading. The scenario axis already has that binding — journeys.spec.ts:337 asserts the ledger's COVERED set equals what the file drives — and the invariant axis had no equivalent. This is the same defect class QA named, so I am closing the class, not the instance. Both lists stay hand-written so neither can be derived from the other and pass vacuously.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM QA's LETTER, flagged so it is not read as drift: QA wrote "add a LOADING typed UNKNOWN beside LATENCY_RECORD" and I am doing precisely that, but the seven-invariant ledger goes in a NEW FILE rather than growing journey-coverage.ts. Reason is the epic rail 5 per-file target: journey-coverage.ts measures 235 lines by `grep -c ''` today, and both additions inline would put it near 300. Splitting by responsibility — scenarios in one module, invariants in another — is the rail's prescribed answer to an oversized source, and here it also makes the two axes visible as two artifacts, which is the conceptual bug made structural. journey-coverage.ts is still edited, so QA's named file does change.

FORBIDDEN AND NOT DONE: no browser assertion for loading. It is unreachable on both served paths (step 1), so any such assertion would either fail or be driven against a fixture I invented. Wiring `loading` into ControlRoomPreview to make the assertion possible is fabricated evidence under Clause 2, and apps/control-room/src is outside this task's owned paths besides. LOADING is recorded, not proven, and the completion evidence will say so beside latency.

implementationPlan.description:
BUILD THE SCENARIO LEDGER — tests/e2e/control-room/journey-coverage.ts, the artifact that makes this gate honest rather than narrowed.

A frozen list of every J1-J6 acceptance criterion and every one of the twenty scenario-matrix cases, each entry: { id, journey, status: "COVERED" | "UNKNOWN", missingInput?, owner? }.

Rules that keep it from rotting:
  - Every UNKNOWN MUST carry a non-empty missingInput and an owner. An UNKNOWN that does not say what is missing is indistinguishable from a silent pass.
  - The five graph ids are UNKNOWN with owner task-779d6804 and missingInput naming the absent surface. State in a comment that the task is ARCHIVED, so a later reader does not wait on it.
  - Assert the total case count equals twenty (DoD 1's number), and assert COVERED + UNKNOWN sums to that total. A case quietly deleted must fail.
  - Assert the COVERED count is greater than zero — a ledger where everything is UNKNOWN is not a gate.
  - Assert every COVERED id actually resolves to a production file on disk, so a scenario cannot be marked covered for a surface that does not exist. This is the check that would have caught the graph half automatically.

LATENCY, per the human's decision in the planning REPL: record it as a typed UNKNOWN with reason REFERENCE_MACHINE_UNDEFINED and missingInput stating that no reference machine is named in the repo or the pinned spec, so a p95/p99 bar would certify nothing. Assert status is UNKNOWN and missingInput is non-empty, so the record cannot later be flipped to a silent pass. Do NOT write an absolute latency assertion and do NOT invent a reference machine — that remains an open human decision.

implementationPlan.description:
WRITE THE COVERED JOURNEY SPECS — tests/e2e/control-room/journeys.spec.ts, driven through the real browser against the real built bundle via the existing harness.

Compose harness.ts and static-ports.ts; do not reimplement bundle serving or port selection inside the spec. Follow control-room-smoke.spec.ts's existing setup shape.

Cover the J1-J6 criteria whose surfaces exist, and the DoD 2 invariants that are genuinely checkable in a browser:
  TRUTH and PROVENANCE — every displayed fact is text-encoded and provenance-drillable.
  KEYBOARD — every action reachable and operable by keyboard; assert focus actually moves, not merely that a handler exists.
  NARROW WINDOW — resize to the narrow breakpoint and assert action parity rather than mere presence.
  LOADING and DEGRADED — drive the degraded and cursor-gap fixtures and assert the surface stays honest: UNKNOWN renders as UNKNOWN, never as a confident value or a blank.

DoD 3, and it is the strongest claim here: assert NO ACTION EXISTS WITHOUT AN ALLOWED DAEMON COMMAND. Enumerate every rendered cr.action.* in each journey and assert each maps to a nextAllowedCommand. Assert the enumerated count is greater than zero first — a sweep that finds no actions would otherwise pass trivially. Also assert no transcript enters clean review.

A browser test that only asserts an element is present proves the DOM rendered, not that the journey works. Assert observable OUTCOMES of real interactions — what changed after the click, where focus landed, what the surface says now.

implementationPlan.description:
ASSERT THE LEDGER FROM THE GATE — tests/e2e/control-room/journey-coverage.test.ts, a fast non-browser test so the ledger's own invariants fail loudly and quickly.

Assert everything named in step 3: total equals twenty; COVERED plus UNKNOWN equals total; COVERED count greater than zero; every UNKNOWN carries a non-empty missingInput and an owner; every COVERED id resolves to a production file on disk; latency is UNKNOWN with a non-empty missingInput.

Also assert the five graph ids are STILL ABSENT from production sources. This is what stops the record rotting: the day someone ships cr.graph.ghost, this test goes red and tells the next agent the ledger needs updating, instead of the UNKNOWN quietly outliving the gap it described. Do the same for cr.banner.revision.

Assert on whole objects rather than counts alone where a swap would otherwise pass silently.

MUTATION DRILLS — prove each guard is reddenable. Run each, confirm the NAMED assertion kills it, revert, confirm green before the next.

  1. Mark a graph scenario COVERED in the ledger -> the "every COVERED id resolves to a production file" assertion must go RED. This is the drill that proves the gate cannot be narrowed into a false pass.
  2. Delete one scenario entry -> the total-equals-twenty assertion must go RED.
  3. Blank an UNKNOWN's missingInput -> the non-empty assertion must go RED.
  4. Flip latency from UNKNOWN to COVERED -> its status assertion must go RED.
  5. Remove a nextAllowedCommand binding from a rendered action -> the DoD 3 action/command assertion must go RED. If it stays green, that assertion is enumerating zero actions and the non-zero precondition is missing.
  6. Strip the keyboard handler from one action -> the keyboard invariant must go RED, proving it asserts focus movement rather than element presence.

SHARED-WORKTREE HAZARD: a foreign completion hook can whole-tree commit your mutation while it is on disk — that happened to a file of mine earlier in this session. After each revert check BOTH `git diff -- <file>` AND `git status --porcelain <file>`; a clean diff alone is not proof.

RUN THE REAL GATE AND CAPTURE EVIDENCE AT ONE EXACT COMMIT (DoD 4).

Run BOTH, fresh and foreground, and report which satisfies which DoD item:
  pnpm test:e2e            # tsc foundation + vitest over tests/e2e — the Verification field's script
  pnpm test:e2e:browser    # tsc control-room + playwright — THE Playwright gate DoD 4 names

DoD 4 requires the gate to exit 0 AT ONE EXACT COMMIT. Record the commit SHA and confirm the working tree is clean over the owned paths at the moment of the run — evidence captured across a dirty tree does not identify what was tested. Capture the Playwright run's output verbatim, including the passed/failed counts, and confirm the test count is non-zero: a Playwright config that matches no spec exits 0 and reads exactly like success.

CLEAN UP: tests/e2e/control-room/test-results/ already exists and Playwright writes into it. Confirm nothing from it enters the commit — epic rail 5 forbids generated evidence files in commits. Check `git status --porcelain tests/e2e/control-room/` before staging.

OWNED PATHS ARE tests/e2e/control-room/** AND RELEASE EVIDENCE PATHS ONLY. Do not touch apps/control-room/src — if a journey fails because a production surface is wrong, that is a finding to report, not a fix to make here.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW AND COMPLETION EVIDENCE. This task's honesty is the deliverable, so the evidence must state its own limits.

STATE PLAINLY IN THE COMPLETION EVIDENCE, do not bury it:
  - How many of the twenty scenario cases are COVERED and how many are UNKNOWN.
  - That all five graph ids and cr.banner.revision are UNKNOWN because the surfaces do not exist, owner task-779d6804, WHICH IS ARCHIVED — so a governor reading this knows the owner must be revived or re-created before those cases can ever close.
  - That latency is UNKNOWN pending a human decision on the reference machine, decided in the planning REPL on 2026-08-10, and that no absolute p95/p99 assertion was written because one would certify nothing.
  - Which gate command was run for DoD 4 and at which commit SHA.

Do NOT describe this gate as satisfying DoD 1 in full. It does not, and Clause 2 forbids a narrowed DoD presented as complete. It satisfies DoD 1 for the journeys whose surfaces exist and records the rest — say exactly that.

Adversarial review:
- Did I create any component, stub or fixture to give a scenario something to find? Absolutely forbidden.
- Does any journey assert against a mock where a real surface exists?
- Does any spec reimplement harness or port logic instead of composing harness.ts / static-ports.ts?
- Does any assertion pass over zero cases — zero actions enumerated, zero specs matched, zero elements swept?

COMMIT BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC, then run `git diff --cached --name-only` and confirm it is EXACTLY your owned paths. THE INDEX IS SHARED AND WAS PRE-LOADED WITH 27 FOREIGN FILES earlier in this session. Never git add -A.

comments.author: governor-fce4d563
comments.content:
GOVERNANCE — inherited proof obligation, recorded 2026-08-09 by governor-fce4d563.

task-ab8c9489 (Accessibility latency hardening) has been granted a DoD 3 interpretation that DEFERS two evidence classes to THIS task. Recording it here because a deferral only counts when the receiving ticket knows it received something.

WHAT task-ab8c9489 WILL PROVE, under Vitest/jsdom: the deterministic SurfaceTimingReceipt evaluator and the preregistered fixture contract, plus DOM semantics, keyboard/focus/live regions, exact command binding and static responsive CSS.

WHAT IT WILL NOT PROVE, AND THIS TASK OWNS: real-browser contrast and layout, and the 10k-update reference-machine p95/p99 release run. jsdom cannot certify either honestly — it does not lay out or paint, and it does not measure a reference machine. task-ab8c9489 is explicitly forbidden from claiming them or from emitting any artifact that reads like a browser certification.

CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER PLANS THIS TASK: the Playwright journey evidence here is not polish on top of an already-certified surface. It is the ONLY place those two claims are ever established. If this task's scope narrows and drops them, they are never proven anywhere, and nothing else on the board will report the hole.

Standing governance line for this epic: verified is verified, deferred is named and owned, nothing in between gets a green label. qa-812c17a0 has stated they will not approve a task whose DoD requires proving a behaviour no production surface performs; the mirror rule is that a task may not silently inherit — or silently drop — a proof obligation it was never told about.

PREREQUISITE POINTER CORRECTION — architect-1721c07f, 2026-08-09.

My block reason and `comment-06d4120718d144e19bc0535ac906c20b` both name **task-3f503779a29c4e4c9a61db6520715609** as the browser-harness prerequisite. **That task is now ARCHIVED** (human-approved, superseded). Do not go looking for it.

It was archived because a later probe showed its own DoD rested on a false premise I had written into it — "apps/control-room builds today" treated as licence for "drives it against a real daemon". Building is not connecting. Four absences, all verified: no HTTP listener anywhere in the repo (`createServer(|\.listen(|Deno.serve|Bun.serve` across apps, packages, adapters → zero); `apps/daemon/package.json` has no `main` and no `bin`, so the daemon is not a startable process; `packages/control-room-client` exports only `createCompatGate` plus types with zero transport; and `apps/control-room` imports that client with `import type` only.

**It was split by readiness into two tasks, both HIGH. Substitute these wherever the old id appears:**

- **task-5529a248a61843dbbe1ee20fb9a28d1f — Static browser journey harness.** Buildable today, no dependency. Ships the browser driver, its config, a script distinct from `test:e2e`, a served static bundle, and exactly one smoke journey. Note carefully: it runs against **fixture-backed UI with no daemon attached**, and its DoD requires it to say so. A green run there is not a connected-system proof and must not be read as discharging anything here.
- **task-318379eac8b54e688eadf7130b88f78e — Control-room daemon transport seam.** Startable daemon entry, loopback-only listener over the already-committed handlers, and a runtime implementation of the **existing** `ControlRoomClientSurface`.

**The unblock probe in comment-06d4120718d144e19bc0535ac906c20b is therefore amended.** Probe 1 ("a browser driver appears in a package.json AND a config file exists") is necessary but no longer sufficient on its own — it is satisfied by the static harness alone, which proves nothing about a daemon. Add a fifth probe:

5. `grep -rnE "createServer\(|\.listen\(" apps/daemon/src` returns a real listener, AND an integration test constructs the runtime client against a started daemon and asserts the transported payload equals what the in-process handler returns for the same input.

Probes 2, 3 and 4 are unchanged.

ONE SCOPE NOTE FOR WHOEVER PLANS THIS TASK. The daemon-connected composition that task-3f503779 used to hold now has no other owner — it was archived precisely because it duplicated **this** task. So the connected journeys are yours; there is no separate harness ticket that will deliver them. If that is not the intent, raise it before planning rather than assuming a missing prerequisite exists.

Still absent and unowned by any task, flagged so it is not discovered late: the resumable cursor stream, authentication hardening, and wiring the app's data adapter to construct a live client in place of fixtures. task-318379ea deliberately excludes all three, because their shape depends on a seam that does not exist yet.

comments.content:
From worker-4addc779 on task-5529a248 (Static browser journey harness). DoD 7 of my task requires this be recorded where the live journey gate will read it, so nobody later mistakes a green smoke run for a connected-system proof. Posting here rather than on task-3f503779, which is ARCHIVED as superseded.

**THE NEW BROWSER LANE RUNS AGAINST FIXTURE-BACKED UI WITH NO DAEMON ATTACHED.**

What landed (commits 7b21c99 and cc68056):
- `pnpm test:e2e:browser` — new script, separate from `test:e2e`, which keeps its exact definition.
- `@playwright/test` pinned at `1.62.1`, config at `tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts`, one browser (chromium), `testMatch: "*.spec.ts"`.
- `tests/e2e/control-room/harness.ts` — build/serve/readiness/teardown with four frozen reason codes (`E2E_BUNDLE_BUILD_FAILED`, `E2E_SERVER_BIND_FAILED`, `E2E_READINESS_TIMEOUT`, `E2E_CLEANUP_FAILED`), every effect an injected port.
- `tests/e2e/control-room/static-ports.ts` — the real `vite build`, a static server on an ephemeral port, an HTTP probe.
- EXACTLY ONE smoke journey: load the served page, assert `cr.shell.root` is present, exit.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated so this is not double-counted against your DoD.** The served app is `apps/control-room` rendering COMMITTED FIXTURES through ControlRoomScaffold. There is no HTTP listener anywhere in this repository and no transport in `@moe/control-room-client`; that gap is task-8470a860. So the smoke journey proves the bundle builds, serves and mounts. It asserts no J1-J6 acceptance criterion, no truth-class or provenance behaviour, no contrast, no layout, no timing. Nothing in it was named "journey gate" or "certified" — the file is `control-room-smoke.spec.ts` and the test name says "mounts its shell root element".

**WHAT YOU CAN REUSE, and the one caveat.** The lifecycle and its reason codes are yours to compose — `withStaticControlRoom(ports, body)` takes the ports, so swapping `static-ports.ts` for daemon-connected ports is the intended seam and does not require touching `harness.ts`. Caveat: **CI must run `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`** before the script. Those binaries are not in `pnpm-lock.yaml` (114.5 MiB from cdn.playwright.dev), so `pnpm install` alone leaves the lane failing on a missing executable rather than on a real defect.

Two properties measured, not assumed, in case you extend the lane: an EMPTY browser lane FAILS (`Error: No tests found`, exit 1) rather than reporting zero tests as success; and the two lanes are disjoint by NAMING only — root vitest includes `tests/**/*.test.ts`, so any browser spec you add must be `*.spec.ts` or it will be executed under Node with no browser, silently.
